Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client or customer for whom quotes are generated within the HelmLogic application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Client entity.

name.description: The full name of the client or company.

contactEmail.description: The primary contact email address for the client.

contactPhone.description: The primary contact phone number for the client.

address.description: The physical address of the client.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the client record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the client record was last updated.

VesselModel.title: VesselModel
VesselModel.description: Defines the characteristics and specifications of a type of maritime vessel (e.g., a specific ship model) that can be quoted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VesselModel entity.

name.description: The common name or designation of the vessel model (e.g., 'Cargo Ship Type A').

type.description: The general type of the vessel (e.g., 'Container', 'Tanker', 'Bulk Carrier').

description.description: A detailed description of the vessel model and its capabilities.

grossTonnage.description: The gross tonnage of the vessel model, indicating its volumetric size.

lengthOverall.description: The length overall (LOA) of the vessel model in meters.

beam.description: The width (beam) of the vessel model in meters.

draft.description: The maximum draft (depth below waterline) of the vessel model in meters.

maxSpeedKnots.description: The maximum service speed of the vessel model in knots.

fuelConsumptionRate.description: The average fuel consumption rate of the vessel model (e.g., tons per day).

Route.title: Route
Route.description: Represents an optimized maritime route, potentially generated by the AI, which can be part of a quote.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Route entity.

name.description: A descriptive name for the route (e.g., 'Rotterdam to New York via Suez Canal').

startPort.description: The starting port of the route.

endPort.description: The destination port of the route.

waypoints.description: An ordered list of significant waypoints or intermediate ports along the route.

totalDistanceNauticalMiles.description: The total distance of the route in nautical miles.

estimatedDurationHours.description: The estimated duration to complete the route in hours.

optimizedByAI.description: Indicates if this route was generated or optimized by the generative AI.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the route was created or optimized.

Quote.title: Quote
Quote.description: Represents a formal quotation for maritime services, including vessel charter and route details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Quote entity.

clientId.description: Reference to the Client for whom this quote is generated. (Relationship: Client 1:N Quote)

vesselModelId.description: Reference to the VesselModel for which the quote is prepared. (Relationship: VesselModel 1:N Quote)

routeId.description: Optional reference to the Route associated with this quote, if applicable. (Relationship: Route 1:N Quote)

quoteDate.description: The date when the quote was generated.

validUntilDate.description: The date until which the quote remains valid.

status.description: The current status of the quote (e.g., 'Draft', 'Sent', 'Accepted', 'Rejected', 'Expired').

totalAmount.description: The total calculated amount for all services in the quote.

currency.description: The currency of the total amount (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR').

notes.description: Additional notes or remarks related to the quote.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the quote record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the quote record was last updated.

QuoteServiceItem.title: QuoteServiceItem
QuoteServiceItem.description: Represents a single line item or service within a quote, detailing specific costs.

id.description: Unique identifier for the QuoteServiceItem entity.

quoteId.description: Reference to the parent Quote this item belongs to. (Relationship: Quote 1:N QuoteServiceItem)

description.description: A description of the service or item (e.g., 'Base charter fee', 'Fuel surcharge', 'Port fees').

quantity.description: The quantity of the service or item (e.g., number of days, units, or trips).

unitPrice.description: The price per unit of the service or item.

totalPrice.description: The total calculated price for this specific service item (quantity * unitPrice).

itemType.description: The type or category of the service item (e.g., 'Charter', 'Fuel', 'Port Fee', 'Insurance', 'Route Segment').

serviceDateFrom.description: The start date of the service period for this item, if applicable.

serviceDateTo.description: The end date of the service period for this item, if applicable.

definition.description: User profiles and metadata. The 'User' entity is implicit from authentication, but this collection would store additional profile data. Authorization is path-based: a user can only read/write their own profile.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the authenticated user.

definition.description: Collection to define global administrators. Authorization for admin actions is granted if a document exists for the requesting user's UID. This is an 'existence over content' DBAC strategy for global roles, ensuring authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of a user designated as an administrator.

definition.description: A global, read-only catalog of available vessel models for all authenticated users. This collection represents master data with a homogeneous security posture (read-all for authenticated) and supports QAPs for list operations.

params.name: vesselModelId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific vessel model.

definition.description: Client records, designed for collaborative access within an organization. Each document includes an 'ownerId' (creator) and a 'members' map (e.g., {uid: 'role'}) for fine-grained, authorization-independent access control for other users. This denormalization eliminates the need for 'get()' calls in security rules to check parent ownership/membership, supporting atomic operations and QAPs.

params.name: clientId
params.description: The unique identifier for a client.

definition.description: Optimized maritime routes, typically generated by AI or user-defined, which are owned by individual users. Path-based authorization (userId == request.auth.uid) simplifies security rules and ensures QAPs for list operations by inherently filtering to the requesting user's data.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who owns this route.

params.name: routeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific route.

definition.description: Formal quotations, owned by individual users. Path-based authorization (userId == request.auth.uid) simplifies security rules and inherently supports QAPs for list operations. The 'status' field (e.g., 'Draft', 'Sent') explicitly models the quote's lifecycle.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who owns this quote.

params.name: quoteId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific quote.

definition.description: Line items for a specific quote. Authorization is implicitly handled by the parent path segments; access is granted if request.auth.uid matches the 'userId' in the path. This structure ensures authorization independence for subcollections, as no 'get()' call to the parent quote document is needed.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who owns the parent quote.

params.name: quoteId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent quote.

params.name: serviceItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific service item within the quote.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for HelmLogic prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability through strict adherence to the core design principles. Authorization Independence is a critical focus, achieved by designing security rules that do not rely on `get()` calls to parent documents or external collections for authorization decisions. This enables atomic operations and simplifies rule logic considerably. Specifically:

1.  **Path-Based Authorization:** For user-specific entities like `Route`s, `Quote`s, and `QuoteServiceItem`s, a hierarchical path structure (`/users/{userId}/...`) is used. This means the `userId` in the path itself serves as the primary authorization context. For example, a user can only access quotes or routes where the `{userId}` in the path matches `request.auth.uid`. This inherently provides authorization independence for subcollections (`QuoteServiceItem`) as their access is governed by the parent path's `userId` wildcard, eliminating the need to `get()` the parent `Quote` document.

2.  **Denormalized Membership for Collaboration:** For collaborative data like `Client` records, authorization context (`ownerId` and a `members` map) is denormalized directly into each `Client` document. This allows security rules for `clients/{clientId}` to directly check `resource.data.ownerId == request.auth.uid` or `request.auth.uid in resource.data.members` without performing a `get()` call to a user profile or any other collection.

3.  **Global Roles (DBAC):** Global administrator roles are managed via an 'existence over content' strategy in `/roles_admin/{userId}`. Authorization for admin functions simply checks for the existence of a document at `roles_admin/request.auth.uid`, avoiding `get()` operations or custom claims.

**Support for Query Against Permissions (QAPs):**

The structure facilitates robust QAPs by ensuring security rules are not used as filters, but rather enforce that queries are properly scoped:

*   **Path-based QAPs:** For collections under `/users/{userId}/`, any `list` operation *must* implicitly filter by the authenticated user's ID because the rules are defined on `match /users/{userId}/{collectionName}/{docId}` where `userId == request.auth.uid`. This ensures that a user can only list their own data, automatically satisfying QAPs without needing complex `where` clauses in rules.
*   **Document-level QAPs:** For the `/clients/{clientId}` collection, `list` operations will require explicit `query.where()` clauses in the client-side application (e.g., `db.collection('clients').where('ownerId', '==', auth.uid)`) or `query.where('members.' + auth.uid, '!=', null)`. The security rules will enforce that these queries include such filters, ensuring only authorized clients are returned, thus satisfying QAPs.
*   **Global Read-Only QAPs:** The `/vessel_models/{vesselModelId}` collection serves as a global catalog, allowing read access for all authenticated users. List operations here are implicitly QAP-compliant as they can read all publicly available (to authenticated users) models without specific filtering.

This design effectively segregates data based on its security posture (user-owned vs. collaborative vs. global master data), making security rules clear, concise, and debuggable while supporting the application's core functionality, including the multi-step quote generation flow.
